intro.data: Optional isn't the only monad. A List is one too: return wraps a value as a one-item list, and bind runs a step that returns a List on EACH item, then FLATTENS all the results into one list. The tray holds three bind machines — one flattens correctly, one forgets to flatten, one keeps only the first tag. Bring the faithful one onto the board and wire it; two cases keep you honest — a list of tags must flatten to one list, and the empty list must stay empty.
intro.alchemy: Optional isn't the only monad. A Bundle is one too: bind runs a step that returns a bundle on EACH item, then COMBINES the results into one bundle. The tray holds three apparatus — one combines correctly, one forgets to combine, one keeps only the first root. Bring the faithful one onto the board and wire it; two cases keep you honest — a bundle of roots must combine, and the empty bundle must stay empty.
intro.spellcraft: Optional isn't the only monad. A Web is one too: bind runs a working that returns a web on EACH strand, then WEAVES the results into one web. The tray holds three workings — one weaves correctly, one forgets to weave, one keeps only the first sigil. Bring the faithful one onto the board and wire it; two cases keep you honest — a web of sigils must weave, and the empty web must stay empty.
intro.abstract: [3,4] is a list with elements 3 and 4; [] is the empty list; return wraps x as the singleton [x]; bind maps the step over a list and concatenates (join = flatten). From the tray bring the bind that flattens faithfully and wire T(A) to T(B); a non-flattening or lossy bind fails the non-empty case, so leave them behind.

goal.data: Bring the faithful machine from the tray and bind the tags to all their articles, flattened — and keep the empty list empty.
goal.alchemy: Bring the faithful apparatus from the tray and bind the roots to all their tinctures, combined — and keep the empty bundle empty.
goal.spellcraft: Bring the faithful working from the tray and bind the sigils to all their spells, woven — and keep the empty web empty.
goal.abstract: Bring the faithful bind from the tray and wire T(A) to T(B), passing the non-empty case (flattened) and the empty case ([]).

afterSuccess.data: Same shape, different monad: bind for List maps the step over every item and FLATTENS the results into one list — and over the empty list, it stays empty. 'Don't Flatten' left a list-of-lists; 'Only the First Tag' dropped branches. Both slipped past the empty case but failed the real one. return = [x], bind = flatMap: List is a monad, just like Optional.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Same shape, different monad: bind for a Bundle draws from every item and COMBINES the results — and over the empty bundle, stays empty. The non-combining and lossy apparatuses failed the real case.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Same shape, different monad: bind for a Web conjures from every strand and WEAVES the results — and over the empty web, stays empty. The non-weaving and lossy workings failed the real case.
afterSuccess.abstract: For List, return a = [a] and bind g = flatten ∘ map g. The same return/bind interface and laws as Optional — monads are a general pattern, not one container.

reveal.summary: List is a monad too: return wraps a value as a singleton, and bind maps a list-returning step over the list and flattens (join = concat). Many container types — Optional, List, State, Promise — share this one return/bind interface and obey the same laws.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: tags.flatMap(getArticles) — map each tag to a list, concatenate into one list.
